To address this gap, we present a unified embodied social
interaction system deployed on the Sophia [17] humanoid
robot. At its core, a multimodal social agent directly rea-
sons over conversational audio and visual observations, aug-
mented with long-term memory, online knowledge retrieval,
and proactive interaction to support both reactive and self-
initiated engagement. An embodiment-aware gesture planner
further translates response intent into verified symbolic ges-
ture programs composed of executable upper-body motion
primitives. To realize these high-level decisions as coherent
physical behavior, we introduce a streaming multimodal
orchestration scheme that synchronizes speech with audio-
driven facial animation and schedules gestures online

User Study.We recruited 20 participants who had no prior
knowledge of our system for each of Q1 and Q2. Each par-
ticipant completed the full evaluation for all configurations
within the corresponding experiment.
For Q1, participants were provided with a predefined dia-
logue script to ensure comparable interaction content, while
retaining the freedom to ask natural follow-up questions
based on the robot's responses. For Q2, participants were
provided with predefined dialogue scripts and were asked to
follow the scripts while focusing on the robot's verbal and
gestural responses.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Blinded human Likert ratings and hardware latency measurements corroborate the system's gains without depending on the internal LLM reviewer or candidate-selection signal.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Blinded five-point Likert ratings from 20 independent participants across interaction and gesture dimensions, plus hardware latency benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: LLM-based candidate generation and review-and-refinement selection over a curated 37-keyframe symbolic gesture library.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported findings in multi-round conversational quality, gesture expressiveness, and end-to-end latency reductions directly correspond to the empirical user ratings and hardware timing benchmarks.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The system is evaluated on Sophia through blinded user studies with 20 participants covering both multi-round interaction quality and gesture generation, paired with statistical significance testing under Holm adjustment, external comparison to an adapted EMAGE baseline, and concrete latency profiling.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Human perceptual evaluations and physical hardware latency measurements corroborate the design choices and system performance without relying on the internal LLM selector.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Double-blinded five-point Likert ratings by 20 independent human participants across multiple qualitative dimensions, alongside hardware execution latency benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Predefined heuristic candidate rules and LLM review/refinement prompts over a curated 37-keyframe symbolic motion library.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly acknowledge limitations including residual multi-second latency stemming from cascaded VLM and facial generation models that preclude sub-second conversational turn-taking, as well as hardware constraints in mechanical facial expressiveness.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, decomposing the pipeline into an agentic interaction planner with skill routing and proactive eligibility criteria, an embodiment-aware symbolic gesture planner with candidate ranking and refinement over a validated keyframe library, and a streaming audio-clock orchestrator paired with physical robot motor retargeting.
primary.quality_rationale: The contribution is substantive and well-scoped, providing an end-to-end operational robotics framework validated with physical embodiment, controlled human subject experiments, and timing benchmarks.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces ARISE, an embodied agent architecture implemented on the Sophia humanoid robot that links multimodal perception, memory-augmented reactive and proactive planning, symbolic robot-native gesture generation, and streaming audio-facial-gesture synchronization.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The contribution is substantive and well-scoped, providing an end-to-end operational robotics framework validated with physical embodiment, controlled human subject experiments, and timing benchmarks.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly acknowledge limitations including residual multi-second latency stemming from cascaded VLM and facial generation models that preclude sub-second conversational turn-taking, as well as hardware constraints in mechanical facial expressiveness.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
